{"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjk1MTM2","is_bot":false,"login":"davidfowl","name":"David Fowler"},"baseRefOid":"4f556f73a610b386e5ec29355a300e493d30c4c5","body":"# Reduce per-render allocations in RazorPage, RazorView and RazorViewEngine

Lazily allocate per-page collections that most renders never use

## Description

Three commits:

- **Lazy collections in `RazorPageBase`/`RazorPage`**: the writer stack, tag helper scope stack, section writers dictionary and rendered-sections set are now allocated on first use, since partials usually don't use them.
- **`RazorView`**: skip the layout list and the LINQ `Any` closure when no layout is rendered.
- **`RazorViewEngine`**: use `Array.Empty<IRazorPage>()` for views with no `_ViewStart`.

No public API or behavior changes.

### Results

MVC microbenchmarks (local BenchmarkDotNet on a noisy 2-vCPU VM, interleaved A/B rounds):

| Benchmark | Before | After | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| HelperPartialAsync | 177,902 B/op | 151,238 B/op | −15% |
| HelperPartialTagHelper | 213,222 B/op | 186,558 B/op | −12.5% |
| ViewResult | 5,968 B/op | ~5,720 B/op | −4% |

Time is neutral to −4%.

### Tests

- Mvc.Razor.Test: 360 pass
- Mvc.RazorPages.Test: 771 pass
- Mvc.ViewFeatures.Test: 2592 pass

### Benchmark (3 interleaved rounds)

This PR now adds `RazorViewRenderBenchmark` to `src/Mvc/perf/Microbenchmarks/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc`. Each operation resolves a compiled view through the view engine, creates the view data and renders it. `HelperPartialAsync` and `HelperPartialTagHelper` each render 100 partials, and `HelperTyped` renders no partials. The existing `HelperPerformanceBenchmark` uses `[IterationSetup]`, so it runs one invocation per iteration and gave unstable time and allocation numbers between rounds. That's why this separate benchmark was added.

| Round | Benchmark | main Mean | PR Mean | Δ time | main Allocated | PR Allocated |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | RenderView [View=HelperPartialAsync] | 91.23 µs | 81.85 µs | -10.3% | 177,408 B | 150,744 B |
| 1 | RenderView [View=HelperPartialTagHelper] | 124.31 µs | 120.03 µs | -3.4% | 212,737 B | 186,072 B |
| 1 | RenderView [View=HelperTyped] | 12.30 µs | 12.61 µs | +2.5% | 20,536 B | 20,304 B |
| 2 | RenderView [View=HelperPartialAsync] | 88.70 µs | 91.53 µs | +3.2% | 177,408 B | 150,744 B |
| 2 | RenderView [View=HelperPartialTagHelper] | 127.47 µs | 118.13 µs | -7.3% | 212,737 B | 186,073 B |
| 2 | RenderView [View=HelperTyped] | 12.79 µs | 12.35 µs | -3.4% | 20,536 B | 20,304 B |
| 3 | RenderView [View=HelperPartialAsync] | 92.24 µs | 83.11 µs | -9.9% | 177,408 B | 150,744 B |
| 3 | RenderView [View=HelperPartialTagHelper] | 124.49 µs | 115.88 µs | -6.9% | 212,736 B | 186,073 B |
| 3 | RenderView [View=HelperTyped] | 13.10 µs | 12.13 µs | -7.4% | 20,536 B | 20,304 B |

Result: partial-heavy renders allocate 26,664 B/op less (−15% and −12.5%) in every round. Time is 3–10% faster in 5 of 6 partial measurements, and one round is +3.2% (noise). `HelperTyped` saves 232 B/op, and its time is within noise.

Setup: BenchmarkDotNet v0.13.0 `--config perflab` (InProcess, MemoryDiagnoser, 3 warmup + 15 measured iterations); AMD EPYC 9V74, 2 vCPU, Ubuntu 24.04 container; .NET SDK 12.0.100-alpha.1.26521.103, .NET 12.0.0 runtime (X64 RyuJIT). `main` is the PR's merge base `4f556f73a6`. `PR` is the same tree with only this PR's `src/**/src` changes applied. Both builds use the same benchmark source. Run order: main, PR, main, PR, main, PR.
